title: The Slow Descent
reflection:
Some months your body still remembers the old rhythm — a heaviness, a turning inward, a day that asks less of you than you're used to giving. You don't have to name it precisely to honour it.

This is not the loss of a season; it is a season, still keeping its own irregular hours. What would it mean to walk gently today, to let the descent be a descent and not a failure to keep pace?
closing: God of the turning way, meet me here in the dimness. I do not need to hurry through what my body still asks me to feel. Hold me tender until the light returns. Amen.

scripture.text: For everything there is a season, and a time for every matter under heaven.

title: What the Body Still Lets Go
reflection:
The bleeding may come lighter now, or heavier, or not on the calendar you once knew — but when it comes, it still asks the same old question: what are you willing to release?

Irregularity does not erase the invitation. Whatever this month's letting-go looks like, however unpredictable its arrival, receive it as the same grace it has always been.
closing: God who empties and fills, receive what is leaving me today, on its own uncertain schedule. I trust you in the not-knowing. Amen.

scripture.text: Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.

title: Some Small Rising
reflection:
Even now, energy returns — unpredictably, but it returns. A morning when the fog lifts a little. A day you recognise yourself again.

Don't wait for it to arrive on schedule before you trust it. When renewal comes, however briefly, let it be enough. It is still the same rising it has always been.
closing: God of small risings, thank you for this returning strength. Let me use it gently, without demanding it explain itself or promise to stay. Amen.

scripture.text: He gives power to the faint, and to him who has no might he increases strength.

title: The Long Waiting
reflection:
Nothing is clearly happening today. No ache, no lift, no signal you recognise — just the ordinary weight of being here, unsure which way the road turns next.

Waiting was always part of the walk, even when the days were counted precisely. It is no less holy now that they aren't. Rest in the not-yet; it is still ground you're allowed to stand on.
closing: God who waits with me, keep me steady in the in-between. I don't need to know what's next to trust that you are already there. Amen.

scripture.text: But they who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings like eagles.
